about_the_game:
London,1993. Rakka clocks in, clocks out, and sleeps in a flat with three equally directionless blokes: Sascha, Björn, and Kev, the other twenty-somethings who’ve mastered the art of going nowhere. 

It’s dull, just the motions, and Rakka learns soon enough what the true meaning of ‘Be careful what you wish for,’ holds. A care package from work arrives with something it shouldn’t: a code. A joke, maybe. A treasure hunt, definitely.

They crack it—and the four of them do what any under-qualified, over-curious roommates would do: they make it a mission. But the moment they treat it like a game, someone else starts playing too. Phone calls that know too much. Monitoring cars in front of their flat. A break-in that feels less like robbery and more like a warning. The take-away: Someone wants the code back. Someone’s watching. And no one is coming to help them unless they hand it over.

With the city turning hostile and help nowhere on the line, Rakka’s curiosity mutates into something insatiable. If people are willing to scare them for this, then it matters. So the four roommates make the only decision that feels remotely theirs: they’ll figure it out themselves. They pack up, and turn their panic into motion—road trip rules, one goal.

Get out. Catch up on the time they’ve wasted. And, somewhere at the end of it, find the thing that’s making strangers act like predators.

Their road trip-mystery starts where a road trip should: a huge festival for all the wrong reasons. From there it’s a spiraling chain of questionable people, worse events, and the kind of uncertainty that makes you doubt your own memory—blending four separate identity crises into one complete shitstorm of travel, unanswerable questions, and “what the hell did we just walk into?”

The deeper they go, the clearer it gets: the code isn’t leading them to a prize. It’s leading them into a story that already started—without them.

RW1S is a story-driven kinetic visual novel fused with point-and-click exploration and a layered mystery that rewards sharp thinking and attention to detail. Players move through the narrative by engaging with complex characters, meaningful dialogue, and hidden clues — each interaction peeling back another layer of the truth at the core of the game. Nothing is accidental; every conversation, glance, and discovery pulls you deeper into the unfolding enigma.

The Real Festival Experience

A large part of RW1S takes place inside the game’s fully interactive festival — a living, breathing environment designed to capture the raw, chaotic energy of a real international music event. As players move between stages and hot-spots, they uncover more about the main cast and the web of characters orbiting them, while being immersed in a diverse sonic landscape that goes far beyond a traditional soundtrack.

The festival features 15+ musical performances by collaborating artists, woven directly into the narrative so that music doesn’t just accompany the story — it drives it.

Rakka distinguishes itself with its breadth of hand-drawn assets, detailed backgrounds, charming character art, and unique paper-cut style. Complimented by the art is the incredible original soundtrack; spearheaded by the minds behind The PMT, it oozes indie charm. Both serve in tandem, dragging the player into the character and dialogue driven world of Rakka. Think you can make it to its thrilling conclusion?

Other Interesting Features

  • Comedy club minigame.

  • Hidden collectibles.

  • Rakkapedia (for specific difficult words).

  • CG Menu including unlockable cut-scenes and comic panels from the game.

  • Unlockable Music library including the original game soundtrack + RAKKA Vol. 1 ALTIMINTAK by GITGOT.

content_descriptors.notes: Includes references to/depictions of: violence (fights), blood, illegal drug use, consumption of alcohol & tobacco and crude humor/sexual jokes expressed in text.

short_description: A homage to the gritty fiction of the ’90s. “RAKKA: WAKE 01 - SOOT” unfolds as a paper-cut style visual novel that blends comics, animation, music and dialogue into a grimey mystery thriller that dares you to dig deeper — even when you really, really shouldn’t.
